about: Persian Cat Room Guardian is a photo of a fluffy white figure that looks like a Persian cat's head attached to a monkey-like body, sitting upright on a box against a brown backdrop. Its arms are spread with palms open, the universal gesture for “what is going on here?”, and its tiny glassy eyes give it a stunned, wordless expression. People call it Cat-Monkey for good reason. The meme uses that pose as a reaction to something unfair, irrational or just baffling, as if the creature has been asked to accept the situation and cannot.
origin: The photo was posted to DeviantArt in 2013 under the title “Persian Cat Room Guardian,” presented as a handmade creature meant to watch over a room, and it was soon cropped into reaction images.
usage:
Set up the frustrating situation across both boxes. The top box starts with “when” or “me when” and describes what happened, and the bottom box finishes with the twist that makes it absurd. The cat's open arms supply the outraged “really?” without you having to write it.

It works best for everyday injustices: being blamed for something, rules that make no sense, people contradicting themselves. Avoid a punchline that explains the reaction; let the pose do the shrugging.
ideas: when you wake up from a nap
and your mom starts yelling at you
when the teacher says “open book test”
and you have no idea why
when the ref gives a yellow card
to the player who got fouled
when your friend says “I'm 5 minutes away”
